note: Every fault the QA owner knows about. A finding stays open until a named check proves the fix. `npm run qa:inventory` counts the open ones.

findings.title: A key press is spent on a pause the original would end by itself
findings.detail: The game empties its keyboard buffer before drawing a new screen (FlushKeys, START.EXE 26b:f6) and after each key (26b:48). The runner blocks at those polls and waits for the player. The key it receives is discarded, so the player presses again. Seen as B twice at Begin Adventuring, E twice for Encamp, and an extra Enter when leaving an area.
findings.source: Owner report, reproduced with a key trace on 2026-11-21.
findings.resolution: The runner no longer asks the player for a key at the game's discard polls (tools/live-input.ts). Under the old behaviour the full campaign replay had 101 of 992 key presses thrown away.

findings.title: The replays press a key until the screen changes, which hides swallowed keys
findings.detail: tools/verify-fresh-party.mjs uses [key, until, limit] actions, and tools/verify-slums-presentation.mjs has `if still on the area menu, press E again`. An acceptance step must press once and assert. Measured on 2026-11-21: 101 discarded presses across the 11 legs of the full campaign replay. The older harnesses now set POR_INPUT_COMPAT=discard-poll-prompt and stay on the old input mode until each replay is re-recorded with one press per input. The presentation replays are unmeasured.
findings.source: Code reading.

findings.title: In Enhanced, lowercase j opens the journal where the game wants the letter
findings.detail: Typing a character name, and the party menu, whose key set is C D M T V A R L S B E J. The runner only exempts jewelry appraisal, Join Tyranthraxus and the disk menus.
findings.source: Side-agent note and code reading. Not yet reproduced in play.
findings.resolution: The page takes J as the journal shortcut only at the exploration and Camp menus, which do not use J. Elsewhere the key goes to the game. Name entry itself is not yet exercised by a check.

findings.title: In Enhanced, lowercase m opens the map and never reaches the game

findings.source: Code reading. Not yet reproduced in play.
findings.resolution: The page takes M as the map shortcut only at the exploration menus. At the Camp menu M opens Magic. Move in combat is not yet exercised by a check.

findings.title: The original's Ctrl key commands never reach the game
findings.detail: The game's key routine (START.EXE image 26f8) acts on Ctrl-S (sound on and off), Ctrl-D and Ctrl-C. The page drops every Ctrl combination. Tab and key auto-repeat are dropped too, and the numeric keypad can never send digits.
findings.source: Code reading.
findings.resolution: Decided on 2026-11-22 from the 1.3 key routine (keyboard unit GetKey, START.EXE image 0x89e9). Ctrl-S (0x13) switches the sound mode at 0x5372 to silent and back: the page's own sound settings offer that, so the page keeps Ctrl keys for the browser. Ctrl-D (0x04, the debug flag at 0x49f7) and Ctrl-C (0x03, quit) act only when ParamStr(1) is 'STING' (the string at 0899:0053); the port starts without it, so the original ignores them there too (classic-sting-mode). Tab (9): no menu or key routine found compares a key with it, so nothing to pass. Auto-repeat: the original takes BIOS typematic repeats as presses, and the page now sends a held key's repeats when the key goes straight to the game (tools/play.js repeatsToGame); send() drops a press while one is in flight, so a held key never stacks up. Keypad digits: the main-row digits already reach the game, and the keypad stays the page's movement keys, as its help line says.

findings.title: A blocking key read with nothing queued returns Enter
findings.detail: src/runtime/dos.ts answers 0x1c0d when no key is waiting. In live play the runner always supplies a key first, so this only fires before the live step. It still needs a check that it cannot fire in play.
findings.source: Code reading.
findings.resolution: Measured on 2026-11-22: booting the shipped game as browser-play.ts does (live from step 24000000, no boot keys) and playing to the first menu, the Enter answer fired 0 times; tools/live-input.ts answers every blocking read after the live step with the player's key. A blocking read at or after the live step with no key ready now stops the game with an error instead of pressing Enter (attachDos takes the live step; the runner passes it). Before the live step a replay still gets Enter, as its recordings expect. checkUnansweredKeyRead in tools/verify-translation.ts fails on the old dos.ts and passes on the new.

findings.title: The translation-wheel check: Classic follows GOG, Enhanced shows the wheel and enforces it
findings.detail: Version 1.3 as GOG sells it accepts any answer at the code-wheel prompt: in overlay slice 2, after the game compares the typed word with the expected one, the conditional branch is replaced with nop, nop, jmp to the exit. GOG ships a separate Windows program, codewheel.exe, as an on-screen wheel. Owner's ruling on 2026-11-21: Classic does exactly what the GOG game does. Enhanced puts the code wheel on screen as part of the game and restores the check, so a wrong word is refused. Established on 2026-11-21 from the first release's code: a wrong word prints "Sorry, that's incorrect." and asks again with a new question, and the third wrong word ends the program. The first release in the port never calls the routine at start-up; why is not established. Built on 2026-11-21: Enhanced shows the wheel at the prompt and the page refuses a wrong word; Classic is unchanged.
findings.source: Read from the 1.3 program on 2026-11-21; owner's ruling the same day.
findings.resolution: npm run verify:code-wheel-screen passes 11 of 11 on version 1.3: wheel shown, right word accepted, wrong word refused, three wrong words end the session, Classic accepts any word, and the display switch works at the prompt.

findings.title: Translate version 1.3 and make it the game the port runs
findings.detail: Owner decision on 2026-11-21. Version 1.3 is what GOG sells and what the walkthrough documents. 73% of our procedures are the same or nearly the same in it, the scripts differ in one place, and the data is identical. The work: translator support for EXEPACK and the FBOV overlay file, a named table of every code and data address the host uses, and the same checks passing on 1.3. Hard requirement from the owner: the narration and artwork work must carry over intact. Measured: of 8,063 artwork keys, 4,023 are keyed by pixels and 2,160 by data files, both identical in 1.3; 1,880 are keyed by script position, and only 60 of those are New Phlan positions after the edit and must move by 3. Of 1,432 narration units, 35 touch the 49 New Phlan source events after the edit; the 1,745 recordings themselves do not change. The journal's 333 text triggers match the game's own words, which are identical. Sound is part of the requirement: the 1.3 sound driver code and most of its data differ from the earlier program, so the 20 Classic events must be decoded, rendered and verified again. Progress is measured by `npm run qa:version-1.3`, which counted 1,044 left on 2026-11-21. On 2026-11-21 npm run qa:version-1.3 exited 0: 846 procedures translated, all artwork keys and narration units working, the sound exact, and ten checks passing on 1.3 including the full campaign. Still to do: make 1.3 the default and retire the first release.
findings.source: qa/research/version-1.3-differences.md.
findings.resolution: The port runs GOG 1.3: `npm run qa:version-1.3` exits 0 (qa/evidence/version-1.3-measure-2026-11-22*.txt).

findings.title: Every launch rolled the same dice
findings.detail: The game seeds its random numbers once at start from the DOS time. The port's DOS clock always started at 12:00:00.00, so the seed never changed and a new game rolled the same character stats every time.
findings.source: Side-agent note on 2026-11-21, confirmed by rolling a new character twice in each mode.
findings.resolution: The DOS clock starts at the player's time of day when the game is played (POR_CLOCK=real, the default for npm run play) and at noon for replays and checks (POR_CLOCK=fixed). The verify chain checks the seed the game's own Randomize stores in each mode.

findings.title: Running from the watch after a night break-in leaves the party one square past the flee square
findings.detail: In New Phlan, running from the watch after breaking in at (10,10) at night left the party on (3,12) facing south. The walkthrough's flee square is (3,11). The script does not cancel the interrupted step on that path, so this may be the original's behaviour or a fault in the port. Three acceptance scenarios stay open on it: flee-squares, guard-run and guard-trigger-closed-building.
findings.source: Found by the New Phlan acceptance tests on version 1.3, 2026-11-21. Not yet compared with the original program.
findings.resolution: Not a defect; the original's own order, settled on 2026-11-22 from the 1.3 bytes and a trace. The main loop runs the script's step event (GAME.OVR slice 3 +0x3453) and then the move routine (slice 3 +0x348d, slice 14 0xd6d), which moves from the position and facing as they are then unless the script set 0x6dc9 to 255. RUN (ECL3.DAX block 0 at aef7) sets a flee square and a random facing and leaves 0x6dc9 alone, so the interrupted step is completed from the flee square in that facing. Traced: RUN, the move routine entered at (3,11) facing north, the party ended on (3,10); the run reported here drew south and ended on (3,12). A run that interrupts a step ends on a flee square or one square beyond it; the notes of acceptance.new-phlan.guard-trigger-closed-building and flee-squares say so.

findings.title: In a loaded game the first shop Buy list opens scrolled down one item
findings.detail: After loading a saved game, the first shop Buy list opens one item down with Prev showing. In a game that was not loaded it opens at the top. The campaign replay already carries a workaround for this ('After the first purchase, the last shop page starts one row later'). Whether the original does the same is not established. 2026-11-21, more places where a list opens with the highlight off its first row, all in a new game that was never loaded: the general store's Buy list opened with its second row highlighted, and the cleric's list of spells in memory (Camp, Magic, Cast) opened with its last row highlighted. The acceptance harness therefore finds the highlighted row by its colour and never counts rows. Not compared with the original.
findings.source: Found by the New Phlan acceptance tests on version 1.3, 2026-11-21. Not yet compared with the original program.
findings.resolution: Not a defect; the original's own code, settled on 2026-11-22 from the 1.3 bytes and a trace of every list call. The list routine (GAME.OVR slice 25 procedure 0xd9a) keeps the list's first shown row in DS:0x6b29 between lists. Start-up sets it to 1 (slice 11 +0x405, c7 06 29 6b 01 00), and the list routine lowers it only to the row its caller starts on (slice 25 +0xe97). Buy starts on row 1, the second (slice 6 +0x37c, c7 46 eb 01 00). In a new game the character menus run lists from row 0 first, so Buy opens unscrolled on its second row; after loading, Buy is the first list, so it opens scrolled to its second item. The spells-in-memory list starts on row 0, the '1st Level' heading; the routine's opening step goes one row up, skips the heading and wraps to the last row. The temple's list of cures starts from an index its caller never sets (slice 4 procedure 0x9d7, [bp-0xc]), so it opens wherever the stack leaves it, in the original as in the port. The acceptance test of the shops now requires the second row highlighted.

findings.title: Messages the game flashes on the bottom line ("Must be Readied") were never shown
findings.detail: In the Slums acceptance test, the party wins a scroll from the four orcs. Choosing Use on it from the cleric's Items menu showed nothing. Established on 2026-11-21: the game does answer. Its Items routine (GAME.OVR of version 1.3, slice 19 at 12ba; first release slice 19 at 12c3) tests the item's Ready flag, and for an item that is not ready calls the message routine (1.3 resident 0xba:0x1693; first release slice 25 at 16df) with "Must be Readied". That routine prints on the bottom line, pauses for 225 ms times the speed setting through Crt.Delay, and clears the line again without asking for a key. The host took a picture of the screen only where the game asks for a key and at pauses it recognised as a fight report, an approaching monster or an illustration, so this message, and every other one shown through the same routine ("Your hands are full!" on Ready), reached neither the test's text capture nor the player's screen in the browser. The game itself was right: the manual (p.9) says an item that is not Ready cannot be used, and the game's item table (file ITEMS) gives a clerical scroll two hands, so the cleric must put away mace and shield to ready it. Readied, Use lists the scroll's spells: Cure Light Wounds twice.
findings.source: Found by the Slums acceptance tests on version 1.3, 2026-11-21.
findings.resolution: Fixed on 2026-11-21. The host now recognises the pause inside the game's two message routines (bindings `messageResumes` and `colouredMessageResumes`, both builds: 1.3 resident 0xba:0x1693 with 42 callers and 0x709:0xd68 with 8, among them the trainer's refusals) and sends the screen as it stands during that pause as a frame the page holds for the length of the pause; the acceptance harness collects those messages as `game.flashed`. `npm run acceptance:slums` (orcs) requires "Must be Readied" on Use, "Your hands are full!" on Ready with mace and shield in hand and again with only the mace put away, the scroll readied with both hands free, and then the list "Spells on Scroll / 1st Level / Cure Light Wounds / Cure Light Wounds" and one spell left after one casting. Without the host change the test fails at the first message. The first release shows the same message through the same routine (seen on 2026-11-21; its pause was 900 ms). Not covered: the pause routine has 27 more direct callers that draw in their own way before pausing; they were not examined (see combat-messages-shown).

findings.title: Three flights from the watch drew matching facing and square numbers
findings.detail: Three observed flights drew (0,0), (0,0) and (1,1) for facing and square, about 1 chance in 125 if the two draws are independent. 4,507 draws from the same generator tested uniform, so this is probably chance. To settle: read how the flee routine uses its two draws, and trace more flights.
findings.source: Found by the Slums acceptance tests on version 1.3, 2026-11-21.
findings.resolution: Not a defect; settled on 2026-11-21. The flee routine is the Slums script at b225: two separate RANDOM commands, one from four numbers for the facing and one from five for the square, each a call to the game's Random with nothing between them; neither is derived from the other. Random is Turbo Pascal's: seed = seed * 0x08088405 + 1, and the number is the seed's high word modulo the range. The port's generator is exactly that one: a search of all 2^32 seeds found exactly one (e299f333) that reproduces every one of the 4,528 draws the flee test traced, in order. For that generator the two draws of a flight are as good as independent: over 2,000,000 random seeds each of the 20 pairs came up between 4.96% and 5.03% of the time and facing equalled square in 20.03% of flights. So a flight has matching numbers one time in five, and three in a row one time in 125. A replay starts from a fixed seed, so every run sees the same three flights, (0,0), (0,0), (1,1): it is one observation, repeated, not growing evidence.

findings.title: Replays that load a first-release New Phlan checkpoint on 1.3 got artwork and narration positions three off
findings.detail: A saved game holds a copy of its area's script: the whole block sits at offset 0x1401 of SAVGAM, and loading puts it back in memory. The host chose the numbering of script positions by the running program, so a slot the first release saved in New Phlan, loaded on 1.3, had three subtracted from positions that had not moved. Measured at the silver shop on 1.3: a new game holds cursor ae6c and caller a9a1 and reported ae69 and a99e; after loading the first release's save the game holds ae69 and a99e, the byte at a692 is 00 (EXIT, the first release's), and the host reported ae66 and a99b, then a9cc for the menu where a9cf is right. Narration failed the same way: the greeting at a964 was not reported. The other direction failed too: a 1.3 save on the first release reported the raw ae6c, a9a1 and a9d2. Chrome replays that start from first-release checkpoints saw this and added keys three lower in 6341e1fe, c7138408, d96dddc3 and 4337e20c; those keys are no longer reported and can be retired. The measure in npm run qa:version-1.3 only compared the two script files and never ran the game. Not a player-facing defect: saves from the first release are not a supported feature (owner, 2026-11-21), and replays for 1.3 should make their checkpoints on 1.3. Still true after the fix, and the game's own behaviour: a first-release save on 1.3 keeps running the first release's New Phlan script (EXIT at a692 after a refused wager, 24 tavern tales) until the party leaves New Phlan and enters it again, when the game reads the script from its files. Measured: after loading, the byte at a692 is 00; after one step into the Slums and one step back it is 01.
findings.source: Chrome replays on GOG 1.3, 2026-11-21; cause measured the same day with the acceptance harness on both builds.
findings.resolution: The host reads the edited instruction of the script in memory to learn which release's copy is loaded (loadedScriptRelease in src/runtime/bindings.ts) and converts by that. npm run verify:script-positions was red before on both builds and passes on both.

findings.title: No check proves that each of the 1,432 narration units is heard at its moment in play
findings.detail: The narration is the feature that carries the story: one narrator reads the game's own text as a dungeon master does, in step with the screen. The existing checks prove that every unit is well formed and that every recording exists. None proves that a unit fires when the game reaches its passage, that it starts on its first print and is not restarted by the prints it covers, or that the next unit waits its turn. The requirement is that every narrated passage is narrated audibly. The measure to build: a count of units heard in play out of 1,432, which stays red until all are. Measured 2026-11-21: the measure exists: `npm run qa:narration` (docs/NARRATION-QA.md), fed by ledgers from runs started with POR_NARRATION_LEDGER. It counts units chosen at their trigger and lists what is unheard by script. It records what the play server is told to play; that the page plays it, and that the next unit waits its turn, is still not measured in play.
findings.source: QA review with the owner, 2026-11-21.

findings.title: The 392 dynamic narration variants are selected by conditions that no check exercises
findings.detail: 69 passages have text that changes at run time (which monsters appear, the tavern tale rolled, proclamation numbers, composed strings). Each case has its own recording, chosen by a condition on the game's state such as: the string in slot 0x9800 is ' GOBLINS'. All 392 variants have a recording on disk (377 files, 8 shared). What is not proved is that each condition matches in play. A condition that never matches is silence at the moment the narrator should say what turned up. 43 more passages defer playback until a later print shows which branch was taken; those need the same proof. The measure to build: variants heard in play out of 392, and deferred selectors resolved out of 43. Measured 2026-11-21: `npm run qa:narration` counts variants selected in play from run ledgers, and `npm run acceptance:narration-dynamic` drives three families until they fire. Defects found so far. (1) Training halls, ECL3.DAX block 11 at a00e, "'WE TRAIN ONLY <class> HERE. DO YOU WANT TO TRAIN?'": the family has two variants, 0x982c == "FIGHTERS " and 0x982c == "THIEVES ". Proved in play: in the clerics' hall at (5,0) the slot held "CLERICS " and in the magic users' hall at (7,0) it held "MAGIC USERS " (the script saves them at 9b73 and 9ba0 and jumps to the same print). No variant matched and the trainer's line was not narrated, in two of four firings; fighters and thieves were. Two recordings are missing. (2) Hirelings, ECL3.DAX block 11 at 9eab, "'THERE IS A FINE <title> WHO WILL JOIN YOU FOR <price>. IS THIS ACCEPTABLE?'" (8 variants): the passage prints two changing slots, 0x982c (title) and 0x9890 (price). Proved in play 2026-11-21 (`npm run acceptance:narration-dynamic -- hirelings`, 1.3): 24 offers in three stays at the hiring hall (7,1), none narrated; the ledger says selector-required every time, because the observer read a family's slot only when there was exactly one. FIXED in the observer: a family that prints several string slots is selected on the whole sentence the passage prints (its literal texts and both slots, read at the trigger, by which time the script has saved both), and the variant recorded with exactly that sentence is taken. The same 24 offers after the fix: 18 narrated by the recording of the sentence on the screen (ACOLYTE, WARRIOR, EVOKER, ROBBER, CURATE), 6 silent because the sentence has no recording. What the script can produce: it rolls the title (RANDOM 250 at 9d03: ACOLYTE below 20, WARRIOR below 70, EVOKER below 110, SWORDSMAN below 140, ROBBER below 170, CURATE below 195, HERO below 220, THEURGIST below 240, otherwise 'THERE IS NO ONE WHO WILL GO WITH YOU') and sets the price from the title alone (9e3a to 9e9e), so exactly eight sentences can occur: ACOLYTE and WARRIOR for 1 SHARE, EVOKER for 2 SHARES, ROBBER and CURATE for 3 SHARES PLUS A PICK OF SPECIAL ITEMS, and SWORDSMAN for '3 SHARES ', HERO and THEURGIST for '4 SHARES ' with no pick of items. For a SWORDSMAN the script never saves the pick; for a HERO and a THEURGIST it saves ' PLUS A PICK OF SPECIAL ITEMS' at 0x9898 and then '4 SHARES ' over 0x9890, whose end mark cuts the pick off. SWORDSMAN and THEURGIST were seen so in play; HERO is from the script (the same path as THEURGIST) and was not rolled. STILL OPEN, three recordings needed, worded as the game prints them: "'THERE IS A FINE SWORDSMAN WHO WILL JOIN YOU FOR 3 SHARES . IS THIS ACCEPTABLE?'", "'THERE IS A FINE HERO WHO WILL JOIN YOU FOR 4 SHARES . IS THIS ACCEPTABLE?'" and "'THERE IS A FINE THEURGIST WHO WILL JOIN YOU FOR 4 SHARES . IS THIS ACCEPTABLE?'". The existing recordings variant-04-swordsman, variant-07-hero and variant-08-theurgist say 'PLUS A PICK OF SPECIAL ITEMS', which the game never prints for those titles: they cannot occur and are no longer selected, so these three offers are silent until re-recorded. The builder's list (tools/build-dynamic-voice-resolution.ts) still holds the three old sentences; when the recordings are made, correct it and take the sentences out of `unrecordedOffers` in tools/acceptance/narration-dynamic.mjs, which until then requires those offers to be silent. (3) Proclamations, ECL3.DAX block 0 at ac22 (8 variants on 0x985e): reported from the 1.3 script as the observer reading the slot at the trigger, before the script saves the number. DOES NOT REPRODUCE: the trigger has a static selector on 0x4ac1, the count of rewards the clerk has paid, which names the number itself for each count, so the observer never reads 0x985e there. Proved 2026-11-21 with no change to the observer: `npm run verify-narration-runtime` sets 0x4ac1 to 1 to 9 with another proclamation's number left in 0x985e and gets the recording for the count each time (CI., CXXVI AND CX., CXXXIV., CLIV., CXIV., CCIV., CXXIX., CCI., CXIV.), and the fixed text for 0. In play (`npm run acceptance:narration-dynamic -- proclamations`) a new party read the wall three times (it is read once per stay in New Phlan, arriving at (3,4) from the west) with 0x4ac1 = 0 and the fixed recording b0-ac22-ac9b was chosen each time, matching the screen. NOT reached in play: the single-number branch, which needs a reward collected from the clerk (the script at ECL3.DAX block 8 adds to 0x4ac1). The defect was in the measure: its row 'Slots read before the script fills them' assumed the slot is always read at the trigger. It now accepts a selector at the trigger whose values are exactly the ones the print can show, and lists any that differ. Not yet seen: what the screen puts between 'PROCLAMATION' and the number; the eight recordings' texts read 'PROCLAMATIONCI.' with no space. Not established: the monster tables of 44 of the 58 string-slot families, most of them random encounters whose script fills the slot in one run and prints it in a later one. Tavern tales, Slums encounters and the fighters' and thieves' halls selected a variant every time they fired.
findings.source: QA review with the owner, 2026-11-21. Counts from src/audio/voice-master-manifest.json.

findings.title: Nothing checks that a passage's picture and its narration arrive together
findings.detail: The narrator says what the party sees and the new artwork shows it: the two are the same moment. The artwork replays check that the right picture appears at each prompt, and the narration checks cover the recordings, but nothing confirms that the picture for a passage is on screen when its narration starts, that both are the same variant where a passage has variants, or that no narrated description lacks a picture. The measure to build: for each narrated passage heard in play, was its artwork showing, and the list of narrated passages with no artwork. Measured 2026-11-21: `npm run qa:narration` records, for each passage heard in play, the artwork key the Enhanced display resolved between the narration starting and the next key wait, and lists the passages heard with none. It does not yet compare the artwork's variant with the narration's variant.
findings.source: QA review with the owner, 2026-11-21.

findings.title: The tavern tale narration was enumerated from the first release's 24 tales
findings.detail: src/audio/voice-master-manifest.json lists tale numbers 1 to 24, with the evidence 'RANDOM 23 followed by ADD 1'. Version 1.3, which the port now always runs, rolls 23. All 23 are covered and the recording for tale 24 is never used. No passage goes unnarrated; the note and the unused recording are out of date.
findings.source: Read from the manifest and the 1.3 script, 2026-11-21.

findings.title: 'DO YOU SEEK HEALING?' is narrated in the Temple of Tempus and silent in the Temples of Sune and Tyr
findings.detail: The three temples of New Phlan greet the party with their own line and then all jump to one shared print, "' DO YOU SEEK HEALING?'" (ECL3.DAX block 0, aa13 in the manifest's numbering). The manifest gives that print to one unit only, por.voice.ecl3.b0-a9ef-aa13, whose trigger is the Tempus greeting at a9ef: its recording says both sentences. The greetings of Sune (a0d0, 'YOU ARE WELCOMED BY PRIESTESS JOY OF SUNE.') and Tyr ('THE PRIESTS OF TYR WELCOME YOU TO THE TEMPLE.') are units of their own that cover only the greeting, so in those two temples the question appears on screen and is never spoken. Found by the narration ledger: in `npm run acceptance:new-phlan` the print at aa13 was reached four times with none of its covering units started (twice after the Sune greeting, twice after Tyr's) and twice correctly as a continuation of the Tempus unit. `npm run qa:narration` lists it under silent cases as covered-without-trigger. The fix is in the manifest and recordings: the Sune and Tyr units must cover the question, or the question needs a unit of its own.
findings.source: Narration ledger of acceptance:new-phlan, 2026-11-21; ECL3.DAX block 0 read with src/lib/ecl.ts.
findings.resolution: Fixed by c18e8c50: 'Do you seek healing?' is narrated at the temples of Tyr and Sune.

findings.title: 142 of 1,747 narration recordings repeated a phrase, spoke their direction aloud or stopped early
findings.detail: Found on 2026-11-21 by transcribing the library with Whisper: 102 repeated a phrase the script says once (one line four times over), 35 said clearly more (33 spoke their performance direction), 5 stopped before the end of the line. No existing check listened. The cause was directions written as instructions ('perform X consistently: ...; retain narrator identity ...'): 72% of those takes were wrong against 2.5% of the rest. Fixed: the generator sends only a plain manner (55 hand-written in src/audio/direction-tags.json), transcribes every take and retries any that does not say its script, and all 142 were re-recorded. A fresh sweep hears 1,730 of 1,747 as their script and none repeating, adding or cutting; the other 17 match poorly on names the recogniser mishears. Not proved: the performance of the re-recorded character lines, which needs listening.
findings.source: npm run qa:narration-transcripts; docs/AUDIO.md, 'Every take is listened to'.
findings.resolution: The generator sends only a plain manner (src/audio/direction-tags.json, tools/narration-direction.ts), transcribes every take and keeps it only if it says its script; all 142 takes were re-recorded and a fresh sweep of the library hears none repeating, adding or cutting.

findings.title: No Chrome check ever played a narration: headless Chrome refused every play()
findings.detail: The Chrome harness (tools/chrome-campaign-replay.mjs) started Chrome with --mute-audio and no autoplay flag, and presses keys through the page's send(), which Chrome does not count as a click. Measured in the harness on 2026-11-21: new Audio('/narration/voices/narration/ecl3/b0-b0b6.mp3').play() rejected with NotAllowedError ("play() failed because the user didn't interact with the document first"), currentTime 0 and paused after three seconds, navigator.userActivation.hasBeenActive false. The player then holds the line as blocked and starts nothing else, so in every campaign and presentation replay the narration queue never moved. `npm run qa:narration` counted those units as heard because it counted what the page was told to play.
findings.source: Probe through openChromeCampaignLeg, 2026-11-21.
findings.resolution: The harness passes --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required. --mute-audio stays: the recordings load and run in real time with the output silenced. The page keeps a playback log (window.porNarrationPlayback) and the measure counts a unit only when the audio element played it to its end.

findings.title: Every passage of Rolf's tour has two recordings triggered by one print: it is read twice, or the unit is cut off
findings.detail: The page plays the recordings of src/audio/voices.json when their phrase appears in printed text (playPendingVoice, tools/play.js), and the runner selects the script unit for the same print (POR_NARRATION). The play server skips a unit that voices.json handles only for text drawn outside the scripts (handledByExplicitVoice, tools/browser-play.ts); for script prints both fire. `npm run qa:narration -- --list` names the 11 units under 'Units that a voices.json recording also speaks': Rolf's eight (ECL3.DAX block 0, b0b6 b1c2 b257 b2f3 b36a b400 b48f b51c) and the temple greetings that end 'DO YOU SEEK HEALING?'. For tour passages 6 to 8 voices.json names the unit's own file, so the same recording plays twice. What the player gets depends on which message the page polls first. Both in one poll (verify:narration-playback pass 1, waiting for every line): the voices.json recording speaks at once and the unit waits behind it, starting 9.2 to 13.6 seconds after it was queued (b1c2 13.6, b257 11.6, b2f3 9.2, b36a 12.7, b400 11.9, b48f 11.4, b51c 10.0) and then reading the passage again in full. The unit first and the phrase a poll later (b0b6 in the same pass and in the campaign opening): the voices.json recording stops the unit 0.1s after it was queued, before a sound, and the unit's 10.8s are never heard. Decide which recording owns these passages and stop the other from firing; the manifest's policy says the units do.
findings.source: Playback logs of npm run verify:narration-playback and npm run verify:campaign-opening in Chrome, 2026-11-21; audio events traced on the page (the /voice/ file's ended event is followed at once by the /narration/ file's play).
findings.resolution: Narration has one source. The nine text-matched lines were removed from src/audio/voices.json on 2026-11-21 (every one is a script unit). The measure's row 'Units that a voices.json recording also speaks' is 0 and turns red if a line is added there for text a unit reads; verify:narration-playback pass 1 shows each tour unit started once, 0.01 to 0.02s after it was queued (0.9s for the page's first recording), with nothing ahead of it.

findings.title: Moving on with Enter cuts the tour's narration mid-sentence and discards the lines waiting behind it
findings.detail: The policy is that the next narration queues after the current one, and the page keeps a unit sounding when Enter is pressed. A voices.json recording does not queue: playVoice stops whatever is sounding and empties the queue. So on Rolf's tour pressing Enter while a unit is sounding lets the next passage's voices.json recording cut it off. verify:narration-playback pass 2, Enter three seconds into each unit: b0b6 stopped at 4.08s of 10.8s (6.72s lost), b1c2 at 3.36s of 13.52s (10.16s lost), b257 at 4.55s of 11.84s (7.29s lost), b2f3 at 3.56s of 9.12s (5.56s lost), all 'a voice line replaced it'. The campaign opening replay in Chrome (leg 1), of the eight tour units: b1c2 cut at 1.57s of 13.52s (11.95s lost), b257 at 6.19s of 11.84s (5.65s lost), b36a at 0.91s of 12.32s (11.41s lost); b2f3 (9.12s), b400 (11.84s) and b48f (11.28s) never started, dropped from the queue when the next passage's voices.json recording cleared it; b0b6 (10.8s) never started, replaced before it had loaded; b51c was still waiting when the leg closed. Not one of the eight was heard whole. `npm run qa:narration -- --list` gives each under 'Units cut off or never started'. Same cause as narration-rolf-tour-spoken-twice.
findings.source: Playback logs of npm run verify:narration-playback and npm run verify:campaign-opening in Chrome, 2026-11-21.
findings.resolution: Same cause as narration-rolf-tour-spoken-twice: with voices.json empty nothing replaces a sounding unit. In verify:narration-playback pass 2, Enter over a sounding line lets it run to its end and the lines sent after it wait their turn and play whole. Legs 1 to 4 of the campaign opening replay (the run was stopped before legs 5 and 6), merged again, have no cut-off or never-started line.

findings.title: Any key but Enter, Space or F10 stops the narration and throws away the lines waiting behind it, whether or not the game takes the key
findings.detail: tools/play.js keydown: `if (currentVoice && event.key !== "F10" && !advancingCoveredPrint) stopVoice()` runs before the page decides whether the key means anything, and stopVoice empties the queue. A key that moves the game on legitimately ends the line being spoken. But the same happens for a key the game ignores at that screen (an arrow at 'Press <enter>/<return> to continue', Shift, Tab), and the lines that were queued behind it are never spoken at all: there is no way to hear them again. And Enter over a voices.json recording (Rolf's tour, the temple question) is not treated as Enter over a unit: it stops the recording and drops the unit queued behind it. The measure counts a line stopped by a key as ended by the player and a line dropped from the queue as never started, whichever key did it. Owner's call: whether keys the game ignores should silence the narrator, and whether queued lines should survive the key that ends the current one.
findings.source: Read from tools/play.js, 2026-11-21; pass 2 of npm run verify:narration-playback stops b36a with the left arrow at 3.02s of 12.32s, a key the game ignores at that screen.
findings.resolution: A key now ends the line only when the game acts on it (tools/play.js: the key press names the reason, send() notes the screen as the key goes to the game, and poll() ends the voice when the game's next frame differs). A key that is never sent to the game (Shift, Tab, the page's own M for the map) or that the game ignores leaves the line and the queue alone. verify:narration-playback pass 2 was red before the change ('a key the game ignored ended the line: stopped (key ArrowLeft) at 1.07s of 9.12s', and the line behind it dropped) and passes after. Consequences to know: the line ends when the game's changed screen reaches the page, not at the key-down; a key the game acts on still drops the lines that were waiting at the key press, and a narration the game sends for the new screen plays next; Enter and Space over a unit still leave it sounding.

findings.title: A replay cannot be the evidence that a passage was heard: it presses on without waiting and its keys never reach the page's key handling
findings.detail: The Chrome replays send keys through the page's send(), not as key presses, so the page never stops or keeps a voice because of them, and they move on as soon as the game is ready. In the campaign opening (six legs, 15 narrations sent to Chrome) 5 played to the end, 0 were ended by a key, 7 were cut off or never started (the Rolf's tour defects) and 3 were still playing or queued when the leg closed its page. None of the 5 had one artwork on screen from start to end: the replay moved to the next screen under the line (the kobold surprise changed picture 2.7s into a 3.1s line; the arms shop line started on a screen with no artwork). A replay shows that a recording loads and runs to its end in Chrome. Proof that each passage is heard whole, at its moment, with its picture needs runs that wait for each line, as verify:narration-playback does for the tour. The recordings total 9,905s for the 1,362 units with one recording and 1,573s for the 379 variant recordings (ffprobe): about 2 hours 50 minutes of speech to hear each of the 1,432 units once, 3 hours 11 minutes for every recording, before any time spent reaching the passages.
findings.source: Playback log of npm run verify:campaign-opening in Chrome, merged into qa/narration-coverage.json; ffprobe over audio/voices, 2026-11-21.

findings.title: A tour passage's narration is spoken and finished before its text and picture are drawn: the frame reaches the page 13 to 22 seconds after the narration
findings.detail: It happens in live play, not only under the harness. Measured three ways on 2026-11-21, after the voices.json lines were retired. (1) The play server started as `npm run play` starts it (real clock, no replay schedule), driven over HTTP with no browser: on Rolf's tour the unit appears in /state 0.03 to 2.9s after Enter and the frame that prints the passage is ready 13.4 to 22.1s after the unit (b0b6 14.0, b1c2 17.3, b257 20.5, b2f3 17.2, b36a 22.1, b400 19.2); in the replay input mode 13.4 to 19.7s. The page cannot draw a frame it has not been sent, so a person pressing keys gets the same. (2) In Chrome, verify:narration-playback pass 1: every one of the eight units started within 0.02s of being queued and played to its end under the previous passage's picture; its own picture was drawn 7.4 to 14.8s after the line had ended (b0b6 7.4, b1c2 9.5, b257 14.8, b2f3 10.7, b36a 11.3, b400 8.4, b48f 10.7, b51c 14.0). The game takes no key in that time. (3) The runner alone (tools/boot-translated.ts with POR_BROWSER_PLAY=1, with and without the portrait artwork list) prints the frame 0.2 to 1.2s after the narration. So the delay is in what the play server adds to the runner or does with the frame, not in the game's script; which, is not established. The machine was busy during all three (load 10 to 30); the earlier harness figure was 7.6 to 10.7s. The owner's requirement is the picture there when the narrator speaks. Either the frame must reach the page as fast as the runner alone produces it, or the page must hold a narration until the frame that prints it is drawn. The measure's row 'Played with their artwork on screen from start to end' now requires the passage's own artwork (from the ledger), so these lines no longer count as having it.
findings.source: tools/browser-play.ts driven over HTTP; playback log of npm run verify:narration-playback in Chrome; tools/boot-translated.ts timed alone; all 2026-11-21.
findings.resolution: Fixed by b8535ed1: the server holds a narration and gives it to the page with the frame that follows it.

findings.title: Enhanced drew the runes the player must translate as letters at three of the game's five rune passages
findings.detail: The game writes words in Espruar and Dethek runes (script opcode 3C) for the player to translate with the wheel and type back. Enhanced draws the game's text itself from a list of character cells, and the host listed any character from 33 to 126 as text without asking which font the game drew it with. A rune reaches the text routine as its glyph code plus 0x40, so every Espruar glyph and the Dethek glyphs for A to E were listed as letters, blanked in the Enhanced picture and drawn in the page's font. Measured in Chrome on version 1.3, 2026-11-21: the guards' list in Valjevo Castle showed `OPABfgABhiOP` where Classic shows HARASH in Espruar, and RHODIA there and on both slips of paper showed its fourth and sixth runes as `}` and `z`. The Sokal parchment had its own rule and was right; the pyramid's NOKNOK was right only because N, O and K are past E. A player could not translate HARASH at all in Enhanced.
findings.source: `npm run verify:runes-readable -- <chrome>` before the fix, 2026-11-21: 0 of 5 places passed. Screenshots of both displays under out/runes-readable.
findings.resolution: The host reads the font argument of the game's text routine. A glyph drawn with the rune font is never text: it stays in both pictures as the game drew it and the frame lists it as `runes` (cell, glyph code, colour). One rule for every place; the Sokal rule is removed. Classic is unchanged. The check stands at all five places in Chrome, compares each rune cell of Enhanced with Classic, requires the glyph codes to spell the word, and types SHESTNI, NOKNOK and RHODIA where the game asks. It reaches four of the places by developer travel, and does not type HARASH or LUX: see the gap on enhanced.code-wheel.

findings.title: From game/ the combat icon editor showed its old and new labels and no icons
findings.detail: The owner, in the installed release (game/, no original pixels): after creating a character, the icon editor showed the labels "old" and "new" and no icon at all. The editor's icons were found only by matching the original pixels on screen. The native combat observer saw the editor's draws (slot 12, rows 2 and 4, columns 1 and 4) but took party icons only from the combat roster, where a character being made is not.
findings.source: The owner, 2026-11-22. Measured with the acceptance harness the same day: 25 key presses through the editor gave 4 icons and 4 selection bevels on every step from the 1.3 files and none from game/.
findings.resolution: 4eee431b: the observer follows the game's icon composer and the editor's recolouring copy into slot 12 and keys each draw from the record's head, body, size and palette, with the bevels. The 25 steps (parts, both colours, small and large) agree; npm run verify:port-parity walks the editor and agrees on every frame.

findings.title: From game/ the 3D exploration view came up on the party menu and on character sheets
findings.detail: The owner, in the installed release: right after finishing the first character the WebGL view showed where the game is back at its party menu. From game/ the menu, a View sheet and camp's View leave the viewport as blank as the blank scenery last drawn there, and the host took the equal pixels for the scenery: perspective, the party's New Phlan pose and 121 tiles of a blank cell, so the page drew the 3D view.
findings.source: The owner, 2026-11-22. npm run verify:port-parity before the fix: frames 56, 57, 58 and 120 of the walk from the title had perspective, exploration and tiles only from game/.
findings.resolution: 50775b19: the video module counts the game's writes to each screen cell, and from game/ the viewport is the scenery only while its cells are unwritten since the scenery was drawn. Those frames agree.

findings.title: From game/ the character sheet's portrait was missing on the roll, the name and View, and a portrait stayed up under lists drawn over it
findings.detail: From the 1.3 files Enhanced shows the sheet's head and body wherever the game draws them; from game/ only on Head Body Keep. And a portrait stayed after the game drew over it: the Temple of Sune's priest under the cures, the arms shop's keeper under the stock.
findings.source: npm run verify:port-parity, 2026-11-22: frames 18 to 25, 57 and 120 (sheet missing from game/), 76 and 116 (portrait only from game/).
findings.resolution: 76531bdb: the native picture observer keeps each held picture's cell write count and drops it once the game writes there; the sheet is asked for on every screen. The walk from the title to camp agrees on all 123 frames.

findings.title: From game/ the first Slums random fights show other monster art, in other places, than from the 1.3 files
findings.detail: In the guide party's walk from the fixture to the orcs (npm run verify:port-parity, walk slums), both random fights differ for most of their frames. From the 1.3 files the monsters are combat:CPIC7.DAX:1 (the picture CPIC2.DAX block 1 also holds), for example at (128,104) and (152,104), with RANDCOM loose stones as combat props (combat:RANDCOM.DAX:1:0:0 and :1); from game/ they are combat:CPIC2.DAX:0, a different picture (block 0), at other cells such as (128,80), (152,80) and (32,80), and the stones are missing. In the attack animations the battle tiles and panel frame differ (animation frames at 79, 83, 84, 90, 101, 104, 105, 113, 118) and the impact effect combat-effect:COMSPR.DAX:11 falls one animation frame earlier from game/ (frame 101). The set fight with the orcs agrees on its monsters. The native observer takes the slot's ready block from the loader and the cell from the draw call; which of the two is wrong for a random fight, and why the cells differ, is not yet known. Measured again 2026-11-22 after the monster equivalence fix (the native observer now takes the art of the same picture stored in another archive when the slot's own key has none and exactly one other key has it): the CPIC2.DAX block 1 monsters now get combat:CPIC7.DAX:1 from game/ as from the 1.3 files. What remains: the loose stones (combat:RANDCOM.DAX:1:0:0 and :1) are combat props from the 1.3 files and only battle tiles from game/, and some cells show combat:CPIC2.DAX:0 from game/ only (frame 55: (128,80), (152,80), (32,80)).
findings.source: npm run verify:port-parity, 2026-11-22: combatArt differs at frames 55 to 78 and 140 onwards; out/port-parity.json lists every frame and placement, out/port-parity/ has the first frame of each as PNG.
findings.resolution: 67197db9 restored the original-data kobold overlays over terrain. 205df8d7 applied the same RANDCOM prop artwork in both modes. A full verified run on 205df8d7 compared 321 frames with zero screen or artwork differences, including all 198 Slums frames.

findings.title: From game/ "A battle begins..." is treated as the battlefield before the game draws it
findings.detail: From the 1.3 files the frame that says "A battle begins..." still shows the 3D view, its tiles and the approaching monsters (encounter:SPRIT2.DAX:0:1:0, :4:1:0) at a Slums random fight; from game/ it shows none of them (frames 52 and 140). At the orcs' fight the same moment shows battle tiles and the battle panel frame from game/ only (frame 184). From game/ the host takes the game's combat state (data.gameState 5) for the battlefield; from the 1.3 files it waits for the battle frame's border in the pixels.
findings.source: npm run verify:port-parity, 2026-11-22, walk slums.
findings.resolution: From game/ the fight is on screen once the game's own frame-glyph draws have put the battle frame's border up (studs at 176,0, 176,176 and 0,176 and the rail at 176,88), the border hasBattlefieldBorder reads from the original pixels. Frames 52, 140 and 184 agree; the Slums walk went from 38 differing kinds to 23, with none new.

findings.title: From game/ the fallen marker is missing in the orcs' fight
findings.detail: From the 1.3 files a defeated orc's cell at (152,104) shows combat:RANDCOM.DAX:1:0:5, the marker the game draws for a fallen unit, for the rest of the fight (frames 185 to 193); from game/ the cell has nothing.
findings.source: npm run verify:port-parity, 2026-11-22, walk slums.
findings.resolution: Fixed by the artist's b6386171, e24fa7bf and 3a2b04ce. verify:port-parity's slums walk on 67197db9 shows no difference in the orcs' fight or after it.

findings.title: On the step from New Phlan into the Slums one frame's tiles name a different area from game/
findings.detail: At the first frame in the Slums (frame 40, the exploration menu at 15,4) every tile has the same hash from both sources but the 1.3 files key it tile:0:<hash> (New Phlan's artwork for that cell) and game/ tile:20:<hash> (the Slums'). From the 1.3 files the tile area is the party's area record, which still says New Phlan; from game/ it is the area of the native scenery just drawn. game/ looks right; the original-file path is the one to check.
findings.source: npm run verify:port-parity, 2026-11-22, walk slums.
findings.resolution: Fixed by the artist's 6aff37b9 (#67), 'Use the destination art scope on the first town transition frame'. verify:port-parity's slums walk on 67197db9 shows no difference on the step into the Slums.
